findings.description: The security group allows inbound TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on a publicly addressable instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploit attempts against the management plane.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and the user_data installs a plain Apache HTTP server with no TLS listener, so portal traffic is transmitted in cleartext and subject to interception or tampering.
Egress permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing no outbound containment for a compromised internet-facing host (data exfiltration, C2 callbacks).

The user_data script exports a static AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. EC2 user data is retrievable unauthenticated from the instance metadata service (including via SSRF against the internet-facing Apache server) and is stored in plaintext in Terraform state and the EC2 API.

No metadata_options block is set, so IMDSv1 (token-optional) remains enabled on an internet-facing instance, allowing SSRF-based retrieval of instance metadata and the hard-coded credentials embedded in user data.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is configured, so unless the AMI or account default enforces it the root EBS volume is created without encryption at rest.

The instance is launched into aws_subnet.portal_subnet_a which has map_public_ip_on_launch = true and a 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway, so it receives a public IP and is directly reachable on ports 22 and 80 with no load balancer, NAT, or bastion boundary.
The EBS data volume attached to the portal server is created without encrypted = true and without a KMS key, leaving stored data unencrypted at rest.
The snapshot is derived from the unencrypted aws_ebs_volume.portal_server_disk and is therefore unencrypted itself; snapshots can be copied or shared, extending exposure of the unprotected data.

The VPC flow log archive bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration, so sensitive network telemetry is stored without an explicitly enforced encryption policy or customer-managed key.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for the flow-log bucket, leaving no account-independent guardrail against a future ACL or policy exposing network traffic records publicly.
The bucket has no policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, permitting cleartext HTTP access to stored flow logs.

force_destroy = true on the flow-log archive allows Terraform to delete the bucket and all stored network telemetry without emptying it first, undermining the integrity and availability of audit evidence.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP, and the associated route table sends 0.0.0.0/0 to the internet gateway, so workloads are internet-exposed by default with no private tier.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true combined with the shared route table's default route to the internet gateway makes this subnet public by default, so any instance launched here is internet-reachable without an explicit decision.
